decks.name: Italian Game (White)
decks.blurb: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4: the Giuoco Piano, Two Knights and Black's odd third moves.

lines.name: Giuoco Piano: c3 and d4
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 c3 Nf6 d4 exd4 cxd4 Bb4+ Bd2 Bxd2+ Nbxd2 d5 exd5 Nxd5 Qb3

notes.5: The Giuoco Piano: Black's bishop aims at f2.
notes.6: c3 prepares d4, kicking the bishop and taking the centre.
notes.10: Now you have two pawns in the centre.
notes.12: Block the check and offer a trade.
notes.16: Open the e-file while Black's king is in the centre.
notes.18: Qb3 lines up behind the bishop against the d5 knight and hits b7.

lines.name: Giuoco Pianissimo: slow build-up
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 c3 Nf6 d3 d6 O-O O-O Re1 a6 Bb3 Ba7 h3

notes.6: Same c3 idea, but you'll play d3: a slow, solid version.
notes.8: d3 keeps e4 safe. The fight comes later.
notes.10: Castle, then Re1 and a Bb3 retreat before ...Na5 can chase it.
notes.12: Re1 supports e4 and a later d4.
notes.14: Tuck the bishop away from ...b5 and ...Na5.

lines.name: Two Knights: 4.d3 main line
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 d3 Be7 O-O O-O Re1 d6 c3 Na5 Bb5 a6 Ba4 b5 Bc2

notes.5: The Two Knights: Black hits e4 at once.
notes.6: d3 defends e4 calmly; no gambits needed.
notes.10: Re1 then c3 sets up a later d4.
notes.12: c3 gives the bishop a retreat on c2.
notes.14: When ...Na5 hits the bishop, Bb5 then Ba4–c2 keeps it.
notes.18: The bishop is safe on c2, still aiming at the kingside.

lines.name: Two Knights: 4.Ng5 d5 5.exd5 Na5
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5 d5 exd5 Na5 Bb5+ c6 dxc6 bxc6 Be2 h6 Nf3 e4 Ne5

notes.6: Ng5 attacks f7 twice (knight and bishop).
notes.7: Black blocks the bishop's diagonal.
notes.8: Take: now ...Nxd5 would allow Nxf7 or d4.
notes.9: The main line: Black hits your bishop instead of recapturing.
notes.10: Check first, keeping the extra pawn for now.
notes.14: Retreat. You're a pawn up; Black has fast development.
notes.18: Ne5 is the safest square. Expect a sharp fight.

lines.name: Two Knights: 5...Nxd5?! (Fried Liver territory)
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5 d5 exd5 Nxd5 d4

notes.7: Black blocks the diagonal...
notes.9: ...but recapturing with the knight is risky: f7 and the d5 knight are both weak.
notes.10: d4! is the strong, safe move: it opens lines toward the king in the centre. (6.Nxf7 is the wild Fried Liver.)

lines.name: Hungarian Defense 3...Be7
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Be7 d4 d6 d5 Nb8 Nc3

notes.6: Take the centre while Black is cramped.
notes.8: d5 gains space and kicks the knight.

lines.name: 3...d6 (passive)
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 d6 d4 exd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 Be7 O-O O-O

notes.5: 3...d6 defends e5 but blocks Black's bishop.
notes.6: Strike in the centre at once.
notes.8: Take back with the knight; you control the centre.

decks.name: Ruy Lopez (White)
decks.blurb: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5: the Morphy, Berlin, Open, Marshall, Exchange and Black's sidelines.

lines.name: Morphy Defense: Closed main line
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Be7 Re1 b5 Bb3 d6 c3 O-O h3

notes.5: 3...a6, the Morphy Defense: the most common reply.
notes.6: Keep the pin idea alive; Bxc6 is the Exchange Variation.
notes.8: Castle first. e4 is only 'hanging' for a moment: ...Nxe4 is the Open Ruy.
notes.12: Bb3 keeps the bishop on the a2-g8 diagonal, aiming at f7.
notes.14: c3 prepares d4 and gives the bishop a retreat on c2.
notes.16: h3 stops ...Bg4 pinning your f3 knight before you play d4.

lines.name: Morphy Defense: early ...b5
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 b5 Bb3 Nf6 O-O Be7 Re1 d6 c3 O-O h3

notes.7: Black chases the bishop straight away.
notes.8: Bb3: the bishop is happiest here, eyeing f7.
notes.10: Same plan as the main line: castle, Re1, c3, h3, then d4.

lines.name: Morphy Defense: Arkhangelsk (...b5, ...Bb7)
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O b5 Bb3 Bb7 Re1 Bc5 c3 d6 d4 Bb6

notes.11: Black puts the bishop on b7 to hit e4 and the long diagonal.
notes.12: Re1 guards e4 against the b7 bishop and the f6 knight.
notes.14: c3 then d4 hits the c5 bishop and takes the centre.
notes.16: d4: now ...exd4 cxd4 gives you a big centre.

lines.name: Open Ruy (5...Nxe4)
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Nxe4 d4 b5 Bb3 d5 dxe5 Be6 c3 Bc5 Nbd2

notes.9: Black grabs e4. Don't panic: you get it back.
notes.10: d4! opens the e-file and hits e5 while Black's king is still in the centre.
notes.12: Bb3 out of the way of ...b5.
notes.14: dxe5: you've won the pawn back and gained space.
notes.16: c3 gives the bishop c2 and supports the centre.

lines.name: Marshall Attack (8...d5 gambit)
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Be7 Re1 b5 Bb3 O-O c3 d5 exd5 Nxd5 Nxe5 Nxe5 Rxe5 c6 d4 Bd6 Re1

notes.15: 8...d5: the Marshall gambit. Black gives a pawn for an attack on your king.
notes.16: Accepting is fine. Taking the pawn is the main line.
notes.20: Rxe5: you're a pawn up; expect ...Bd6 and ...Qh4 against your king.
notes.22: d4 frees your bishop on c1 to defend.
notes.24: Re1 retreats before ...Bxe5. Next, meet ...Qh4 with g3.

lines.name: Modern Steinitz (4...d6)
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 d6 c3 Bd7 d4 Nf6 O-O Be7 Re1 O-O

notes.7: Black defends e5 with a pawn first.
notes.8: c3 and d4: build the classic centre.
notes.12: Castle, then Re1. You keep a comfortable space edge.

lines.name: Exchange Variation (4.Bxc6)
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Bxc6 dxc6 O-O f6 d4 exd4 Nxd4 c5 Nb3 Qxd1 Rxd1

notes.6: 4.Bxc6 swaps the bishop to damage Black's pawns. A solid alternative to 4.Ba4 (about equal).
notes.8: Castle. Don't take e5 yet: ...Qd4 would win it back.
notes.10: d4 opens the centre while Black's king is uncastled.
notes.16: After the queens come off, your 4-v-3 kingside majority is the long-term trump.

lines.name: Berlin: 4...Nxe4 5.Re1 (the Rio Gambit trick)
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nf6 O-O Nxe4 Re1 Nf6 Nxe5 Nxe5 d4 c6 dxe5 Nd5 Bc4

notes.12: d4! (not Rxe5+, which you played twice). The e5 knight is pinned to the king on e8 by your rook, so it can't run.
notes.14: Collect the knight. You're a piece up (+2.2).
notes.16: Bc4 hits the d5 knight. Clean win of material.

lines.name: Berlin: 5.d4 (the Berlin endgame)
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nf6 O-O Nxe4 d4 Nd6 Bxc6 dxc6 dxe5 Nf5 Qxd8+ Kxd8 Nc3

notes.8: 5.d4 is the main line: hit the centre right away.
notes.10: Bxc6 then dxe5: the knight on d6 has to move.
notes.14: Queens off. Black has the two bishops; you have the better pawns and Black's king can't castle.
notes.16: Nc3, then h3, Rd1 and Ne2-f4 or Bg5.

lines.name: Berlin: 4...Bc5
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nf6 O-O Bc5 Nxe5 Nxe5 d4 a6 Be2 Bxd4 Qxd4 d6 Nc3

notes.7: Black develops the bishop instead of taking e4.
notes.8: Nxe5! The fork trick: d4 is coming.
notes.10: d4 forks the bishop and the e5 knight. You win the piece back with a big centre.
notes.16: Nc3: about +1.2. You have the bishop pair and space.

lines.name: Berlin: 4...a6
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nf6 O-O a6 Bxc6 dxc6 Nxe5 Nxe4 Re1

notes.8: Bxc6 removes the knight that guards e5...
notes.12: Re1 hits the e4 knight. If 7...Nf6??, 8.Nxc6+ is a discovered check that wins the queen.

lines.name: Steinitz Defense (3...d6)
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 d6 d4 Bd7 Nc3 Nf6 Bxc6 Bxc6 Qd3 exd4 Nxd4

notes.5: 3...d6 is passive: it shuts in Black's bishop.
notes.10: Bxc6 and Qd3 keep up the pressure: Black has to give up the centre with ...exd4.
notes.14: You have more space and easy development (+0.75).

lines.name: Classical 3...Bc5
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Bc5 c3 Nf6 O-O O-O d4 Bb6 Re1

notes.6: c3 prepares d4 to hit the c5 bishop.
notes.10: d4 gains time on the bishop.
notes.12: Re1 holds e4. White is a little better.

lines.name: Schliemann 3...f5
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 f5 d3 fxe4 dxe4 Nf6 O-O Bc5 Nc3 d6

notes.6: d3 is the calm answer: no theory battle.
notes.8: Recapture and castle. Black's kingside is loosened.

lines.name: Bird 3...Nd4
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nd4 Nxd4 exd4 O-O c6 Bc4 Nf6 Re1 d6 c3

notes.6: Take the knight: the d4 pawn it leaves behind is a target.
notes.8: Castle; if ...c6, Bc4 keeps the bishop active.

lines.name: Cozio 3...Nge7
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nge7 c3 a6 Ba4 d6 d4 Bd7 O-O

notes.5: The knight goes to e7, ready for ...g6 or ...Ng6.
notes.6: c3 then d4: same central plan as always.

lines.name: 3...Bd6 (odd bishop move)
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Bd6 O-O Nf6 d4

notes.8: d4: open the centre and punish the clumsy bishop (+1.4).

decks.name: 1...e5 vs the Italian (Black)
decks.blurb: Black's answers to 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 and its cousins: the lines you face most as Black.

lines.name: Giuoco Piano: 4.c3 Nf6 5.d4
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 c3 Nf6 d4 exd4 cxd4 Bb4+ Bd2 Bxd2+ Nbxd2 d5 exd5 Nxd5

notes.5: The Giuoco Piano: develop toward f2.
notes.7: Hit e4 so d4 comes at a cost.
notes.15: d5! hits the centre: the key freeing move.
notes.17: Equal. Your knight is strong on d5.

lines.name: Giuoco Pianissimo: 4.d3
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 d3 Nf6 O-O d6 c3 O-O h3 a6

notes.7: Develop with a hit on e4.
notes.11: Castle and compare plans: ...a6 and ...Ba7 to keep the bishop.
notes.13: a6 makes room for ...Ba7 so the bishop can't be traded off by Na4.

lines.name: 4.O-O
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 O-O Nf6 d3 d6 c3 O-O

notes.7: Develop with a hit on e4.

lines.name: 4.Ng5?? hangs the knight
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 Ng5 Qxg5

notes.6: Ng5 attacks f7, but the knight is undefended.
notes.7: Take it! Your queen can reach g5 along the d8–g5 diagonal. You're a piece up.

lines.name: Four Knights Italian: the fork trick
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Nc3 Nf6 Bc4 Nxe4 Nxe4 d5 Bd3 dxe4 Bxe4 Bd6

notes.6: The Four Knights Italian. You've scored poorly here.
notes.7: The fork trick: take e4...
notes.9: ...then d5 forks the bishop and the knight.
notes.13: Equal, and White has no Ng5 tricks against f7.

lines.name: Scotch Gambit 4.d4
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 d4 Bxd4 Nxd4 Nxd4 O-O d6

notes.7: Take with the bishop.
notes.11: A pawn up. Keep it solid with ...d6, ...Nf6 and castle.

lines.name: Bishop's Opening 2.Bc4
lines.moves: e4 e5 Bc4 Nf6 d3 c6 Nf3 d5 Bb3 Bd6

notes.7: Take the centre.
notes.9: Protect e5. Black has a good centre.

decks.name: Sicilian Defense (Black)
decks.blurb: 1.e4 c5 with ...d6 and ...Nf6: the Najdorf setup plus answers to White's anti-Sicilians.

lines.name: Open Sicilian: Najdorf 6.Be2
lines.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 Be2 e5 Nb3 Be7 O-O O-O

notes.7: Hit e4 so Nc3 is forced.
notes.9: a6: the Najdorf. It stops Nb5 and Bb5 and prepares ...e5 or ...b5.
notes.11: Kick the knight and take space.

lines.name: Open Sicilian: Najdorf 6.Bg5
lines.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 Bg5 e6 f4 Be7 Qf3 Qc7

notes.11: e6 against Bg5: unpins safely and covers d5.
notes.15: Qc7 watches e5 and the c-file. Castle next.

lines.name: Moscow 3.Bb5+
lines.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 Bb5+ Bd7 Bxd7+ Qxd7 O-O Nc6 c3 Nf6 Re1 e6

notes.4: The Moscow Variation: White avoids theory.
notes.7: Take with the queen; it connects your rooks.

lines.name: Alapin 2.c3
lines.moves: e4 c5 c3 Nf6 e5 Nd5 d4 cxd4 cxd4 d6 Nf3 Nc6

notes.5: The knight is happy on d5.
notes.7: Swap in the centre.

lines.name: Grand Prix 2.Nc3 and f4
lines.moves: e4 c5 Nc3 d6 f4 Nc6 Nf3 g6 Bb5 Bd7 O-O Bg7

notes.4: The Grand Prix: White plans a kingside attack.
notes.7: Fianchetto: the bishop on g7 counters on the long diagonal.

lines.name: Smith-Morra Gambit 2.d4
lines.moves: e4 c5 d4 cxd4 c3 dxc3 Nxc3 Nc6 Nf3 d6 Bc4 e6 O-O Nf6

notes.7: Develop.
notes.13: A pawn up; finish development and castle.

lines.name: Advance: 3.e5 Bf5 4.Nf3
lines.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 Nf3 e6 Be2 c5 O-O Nc6

notes.5: Develop the light-squared bishop before ...e6 locks it in.
notes.7: Now ...e6.
notes.9: c5 hits White's pawn chain at its base.

lines.name: Advance: 4.Nc3 e6 5.g4
lines.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 Nc3 e6 g4 Bg6 Nge2 c5

notes.7: Solid.

lines.name: Classical: 3.Nc3 dxe4 4.Nxe4 Bf5
lines.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5 Ng3 Bg6 h4 h6 Nf3 Nd7 h5 Bh7

notes.7: The Classical: develop the bishop with tempo.
notes.11: h6 so h5 doesn't trap the bishop.

lines.name: Exchange: 3.exd5
lines.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 Bd3 Nc6 c3 Nf6 Bf4 Bg4

notes.7: Develop.
notes.11: Bishop outside the pawn chain before ...e6.

lines.name: Panov: 3.exd5 cxd5 4.c4
lines.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 c4 Nf6 Nc3 e6 Nf3 Be7

notes.7: Develop.

lines.moves: e4 c6 Nc3 d5 Nf3 Bg4 h3 Bxf3 Qxf3 e6

notes.7: Trade it before g4 chases the bishop.
